reason: The first flight needs a restraint, so I’ll attach the low test tether before trying to lift the whale.
expectation: The tether will limit how high the whale can rise during the test.

alternatives.reason: The cradle also looks important for a safe low test.

effect: The whale is now tethered for the low flight test; it still needs a padded landing place and balance checks.
reaction: The restraint is a reassuring first step.
reason: The padded cradle should protect the whale when it comes down.
expectation: The cradle will be positioned beneath the tethered whale for the test.

effect: The whale now has a padded landing area as well as a tether.
reaction: That makes the low test feel more prepared.
reason: The long control lead should let us operate the lift during the test.
expectation: The lead will connect the lift controls for the low flight test.

effect: The first hover revealed that the dragon end is too heavy, so the whale needs balancing before further testing.
reaction: The uneven hover makes the purpose of the counterweight clear.
reason: The counterweight adjustment handle should let me correct the nose-heavy balance.
expectation: Adjusting the counterweight will bring the whale closer to level.

effect: The counterweight adjustment has rebalanced the whale; the bubble level can help check it.
reason: The bubble level should verify that the hovering whale is level.
expectation: The level will show whether the counterweight adjustment has balanced the whale.

effect: The bubble confirms the whale now hovers level; the emergency stop still needs testing.
reaction: It is satisfying that the ordinary counterweight corrected the uneven lift.
reason: The stop cord and pivoted lever should let me test the whale’s exterior emergency stop.
expectation: Pulling the cord will operate the stop and cut power to the lift tile.

effect: The stop cord successfully cut lift, completing the test. I also learned that an emergency drop differs from a controlled landing.
reaction: The distinction between stopping and landing was useful and a little surprising.

mostWorthwhile.text: Finding the nose-heavy hover and correcting it made the counterweight’s purpose clear; the level then confirmed the result.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the tether and placing the cradle were sensible preparations, but straightforward compared with diagnosing the balance.

surprise.text: The emergency stop drops the whale rather than landing it gently; a gradual reduction in current is needed for a landing.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary: each action had a clear role in preparing, balancing, or stopping the test.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see the balanced whale fly with its attractions working, especially after learning how its safety and balance systems work.
